tool_args.rationale: The fixed-H baseline response saturates with u_now, while the two acquired low/high-s_grad measurements strongly suppress y as the gradient rises. The verified W3 bridge maps to the C-source two-layer siphon, whose saturating flux is gradient-inhibited and has an open square-root branch. Fit its three parameters numerically on all seven paid rows; retain only the branch consistent with fresh confirmation.

considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: The prior probe already varied s_grad substantially and produced seven rows; the strong gradient contrast identifies the siphon inhibition and the existing range can estimate its open-branch coefficient.

considered_alternatives.option: Fit the two-state memory ODE or dual-horizon adaptation model
considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: All observations have H=0.6 and the archive says these require at least eight rows or a slow-horizon probe; those temporal parameters are not identifiable here and are not needed to fit the observed single-horizon law.

considered_alternatives.option: Use a static saturating response with an independent linear gradient term
considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: Fresh confirmation refuted the earlier saturation-plus-gradient model, while the verified bridge mechanism and gradient signature support the nonlinear two-layer siphon form.

considered_alternatives.option: Use the negative linear-leak branch or nuisance_high_var_aux
considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: The open branch is constrained by the confirming fit; an additional branch-discriminating reading is not presently necessary, and the nuisance auxiliary is explicitly irrelevant.
